operative_text:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-2(g)): (5) A firearms training or safety course or class conducted by a state certified firearms instructor or a certified military firearms instructor that provides, at a minimum, all of the training of a safety course or class described in paragraph (4) and also provides a total of at least sixteen hours of additional training in: (A) Properly carrying weapons in public; (B) Situation de-escalation; (C) Interaction with law enforcement; and (D) The proper use of a weapon as a last resort.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9(a)): (2) Six months from the date of issue if the license was issued on an initial or renewal basis after June 30, 2022.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9(b)): (1) Be qualified to use the firearm in a safe manner, as evidenced by documentation showing successful completion by the person of a firearms safety or training course or class approved by the chief of police of the appropriate county and as described in section 134-2(g)(5); provided that the person shall have completed the course within thirty days before applying for or renewing a license;
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9(b)): (5) Also carry on the person an electric gun, as defined in section 134-1, which is intended to be non-lethal by design, whenever the licensee carries a pistol or revolver pursuant to the license.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9(c)): If a licensee violates any requirement relating to the license, the chief of police who issued the license shall revoke the license.
